1361.11: Phunhe, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The pen is in the hand of the Inaccessible; (he) writes (the destiny) on (every) forehead. He of incomparable beauty is entwined with all. (O God,) your praise cannot be told by the mouth. Beholding your sight, Nanak is enraptured, and is a sacrifice (to you). ॥1॥
Phunhe (from phuni, again and again): verses in which a word returns again and again; in these stanzas it is Harihan, which opens the last line of most of them.
Harihan is a call to the Lord (Hari) sung to the measure; it is not rendered.
1361.12: Sitting in the assembly of the Sants, let me utter (the Lord's) praise; let me offer (him) all (my) adornment, and give (him) all this soul (of mine). Thirsting with hope, let that bed be spread for the Husband. If good fortune is on the forehead, the Friend is found. ॥2॥
1361.13: O friend, kajal, a necklace, betel leaf: all of it (I) have made ready; (I) have put on the sixteen adornments, and lined (my eyes) with collyrium. If the Husband comes home, then everything is attained; without the Husband, all adornment goes to waste. ॥3॥
The sixteen adornments (solah singar): the full adornment of a bride, from the bath and the dress to the jewels, kajal and henna.
1361.14: She in whose home the Husband has come to dwell is greatly fortunate. On her all adornment looks well; she alone is the happy wedded bride. Free of care, I sleep (in peace); the hope in (my) mind is fulfilled. When the Husband came home, then everything was attained. ॥4॥
1362.1: This is all my hope: that (my) hope (of meeting him) be fulfilled. When the True Guru has become merciful, the Perfect (Lord) is found. In my body are many faults, so many that faults have overspread (it); when the True Guru became merciful, (my) mind was held still. ॥5॥
1362.2: Says Nanak, (I) have meditated on the Infinite, the Infinite (Lord). Hard to cross is this world (-ocean); the True Guru has ferried (me) over. (My) coming and going ended when (I) found the Perfect (Lord). (I) have obtained the Lord's Amrit Name from the True Guru. ॥6॥
1362.3: In my hand is the lotus (the mark of good fortune); in (my) courtyard is the fragrance of peace. O friend, at my throat is a jewel; seeing it, sorrow is dispelled. I dwell with Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), the Lord, the treasure of all comforts, in whose hand the riddhis and siddhis (wealth and miraculous powers) and the nine treasures ever dwell. ॥7॥
1362.4: Those who go to enjoy another's woman are then put to shame. (Those who) day after day steal another's wealth: where can their faults be hidden? Dwelling on the Lord's virtues, (one) is made pure and carries all (one's) family across. Those who hear (the one) who reflects on the Supreme Lord have become pure. ॥8॥
1362.5: Above, the sky looks fine; below, the earth is lovely; in the ten directions the lightning flashes, gleaming upon (my) face. I wander in foreign lands searching: where may the Beloved be found? If good fortune is on the forehead, one merges in the sight of him. ॥9॥
1362.6: (O Ramdaspur,) I have seen all places; there is none like you. The Primal Being, the Creator, has founded you; that is why you are beautiful. Ramdaspur is thickly settled, boundless and beyond compare. O Nanak, by bathing in the pool of Ramdas, sins depart. ॥10॥

Ramdaspur: the city of Guru Ram Das Ji, Amritsar, founded by Guru Ram Das Ji and named after him. The pool of Ramdas (Ramdas Sarovar): the sacred pool at Amritsar, begun by Guru Ram Das Ji and named after him.
1362.7: Like the chatrik (rain-bird), with an alert mind, one should long for that Friend; one should yearn for the very one to whom one's life is bound. For one drop of water (the chatrik) roams forest after forest, forlorn. Even so the Lord's servant asks for the Naam; Nanak is a sacrifice (to such a one). ॥11॥
The chatrik (rain-bird, the pied cuckoo) is held in Indian poetry to drink only the raindrop that falls under the Swati star, and no other water.
1362.8: The mind of the Friend is beyond compare; its secret cannot be known. Through the buyers of the Boundless One's virtues, that essence is recognised. When the mind merges in (his) mind, the joy is deep; Killing the restless thief (the mind), you will then gain the true wealth. ॥12॥
1362.9: In a dream I rose up; why did I not grasp (his) hem? Seeing the beautiful Being, resplendent, (my) mind was beguiled. I search for his feet; tell (me), where may he be found? O friend, tell me that very effort by which the Beloved is found. ॥13॥
1362.10: The eyes that do not see the Saadhs (the holy): those eyes are wretched. The ears that do not hear the Naad (the sound of the Lord's praise): those ears are sealed shut. The tongue that does not repeat the Naam should be cut away, bit by bit. When Gobind (the Lord of the universe), the King, is forgotten, one wastes away day by day. ॥14॥
1362.11: In the lotus the (bee's) wings are caught, bound by its heady fragrance; tangled in its petals, it forgets its flight. Is there any such friend who can break this hard knot? O Nanak, the One, Sridhar the Master, alone joins again those who have broken away. ॥15॥
Sridhar (he who holds Sri, Lakshmi): a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani, a name of God.
1363.1: I run in many directions for the love of God; the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) torment (me): by what means are they to be killed? Loosing sharp arrows, one should meditate on God's Name; these great troublemakers are slain when the Perfect Guru is found. ॥16॥
1363.2: The gift the True Guru has given never runs out at all. Eat it and enjoy it, all of you; the Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) is set free. The Lord, being pleased, has given the treasure of the Amrit Name. Says Nanak, worship (him) for ever, and you will never die. ॥17॥
1363.3: Wherever the devotee goes, that place is lovely. All comforts come by meditating on the Lord's Name. Beings raise cries of acclaim; the slanderers burn and die. O Nanak, by repeating the Naam, the friends (of God) have bliss in their minds. ॥18॥
1363.4: The Pure One, who makes the fallen holy, is never served; ruined in false love, how long can (the boat of life) be rowed? Seeing the city of Harichand, why have (you) taken it for happiness? I am a sacrifice to those who are known in the Lord's court. ॥19॥
The city of Harichand (Harichandauri): a city seen in the sky, a mirage that vanishes as one draws near.
1363.5: The fool has done many deeds, evils in plenty. The wicked one dwells in great stench; (his) body is ashes. He wanders in the darkness of pride, and is unaware of death. Seeing the city of Harichand, why does he take it to be true? ॥20॥
1363.6: One whose span (of life) is complete: who can save him? How far can the physician go on naming his many remedies? O fool, remember the One alone; he will be of use to you. Without the Name the body is ashes; all goes to waste. ॥21॥
1363.7: The Naam is a medicine, boundless and priceless: let it be drunk. Meeting together, the Sants eat it, and it is given to all. It comes only to the one who is destined to receive it. I am a sacrifice to those who enjoy the Lord's love. ॥22॥
1363.8: The company of the physicians has gathered together; the medicines have taken effect, (for the Lord) himself has stood in their midst. Whatever deeds they do become good deeds and spread far. Sufferings, diseases and all sins have slipped away from the body. ॥23॥
